decisions.reason: The easy-to-assemble constraint is already captured from the same message; the added drop-retention constraint is an independent behavior and does not change assembly usability.
Securing components against a drop does not change the enclosure's required board count or battery capacity.
The drop-retention decision does not alter the specified sensor air inlet or top outlet locations.
The general retention constraint does not change the display cutout, cover-only mounting location, connection usability, cover installation requirement, or unresolved display size.
Securing components against drops does not select or modify either permitted LED light-path method.
The enclosure-level retention constraint does not change the sensor board's orientation, connector alignment, or component-placement rules.
The source adds an enclosure retention requirement but does not modify the main board's dimensions, orientation, connector placement, or cable-access layout.
The existing power-board orientation, mounting-hole, size, and connector-layout constraints remain valid unchanged; the broad drop-retention requirement is owned by the source Requirement.
The enclosure drop-retention decision has no effect on I2C series-resistor values, placement, purpose, or population policy.
The source does not change the battery connector's electrical specification, placement, orientation, mounting style, or unresolved pinout.
The enclosure retention requirement does not affect cable length, clock speed, pull-ups, or I2C series resistors.
Securing enclosure components against drops does not change the main-board connector count, connector destinations, types, or retained modular connector architecture.
